topic: 3 security mistakes developers make when deploying a website to production, and how to avoid them
postText:
I’ve seen a lot of sites go live and then get tripped up by three pretty common security slip‑ups.

First, we ship debug tools or default credentials straight into production. A quick sweep for .env files, admin panels, and obvious passwords before the merge can save a lot of headaches.

Second, we forget to lock down our APIs. Open endpoints are a playground for scanners, as the recent “VoidAccess” project reminds us. Using proper authentication, rate limiting, and a whitelist of allowed origins makes a huge difference.

Third, we ignore proper TLS settings and rely on the default certs. Even a self‑signed cert can expose users to man‑in‑the‑middle attacks. Switch to a reputable CA and enable strong ciphers before the first request hits your site.

#websecurity #devops #infosec
